client_alerts.headline: Windows malware is sending stolen victim data to Claude to rank targets
client_alerts.body: Researchers found Windows malware that sends stolen data to Claude to decide which victims to go after first, and **switches to another model if one refuses**. For clients, egress to LLM API endpoints from endpoints that should never call them is now an exfiltration indicator. Add it to DLP/egress monitoring and to ransomware tabletop injects.

top_moves.title: Mistral Large 4 ships as open weights: 1T parameters, runs on-prem
top_moves.body: The open-weight release Mistral promised for late October landed on Hugging Face: 1T total / 52B active parameters, natively multimodal, trained in Mistral's European data centres and pitched for self-hosted coding and cyber defence. It is the first credible frontier-class option for regulated clients who cannot send data to a US cloud API.

top_moves.title: Malware now uses commercial LLMs to triage stolen data
top_moves.body: Researchers found Windows malware that ships victim data to Claude to rank targets and swaps models when one refuses. Provider refusals are no longer a dependable control, so egress to LLM APIs belongs in detection.

top_moves.title: Goldman Sachs pulls Claude Code back to engineers only
top_moves.body: After months of traders and bankers using agentic coding tools, Goldman restricted Claude Code and similar tools to engineering staff. Expect regulated clients to follow with role-based AI tool access, which is a governance and BIA-scoping conversation to have now.

providers.name: OpenAI
providers.headline: Launched Grid Protectors, a data-centre power-curtailment program for grid emergencies, plus the LifeVal everyday-tasks benchmark.
providers.detail: Grid Protectors would let OpenAI cut data-centre demand during grid emergencies; a planned Georgia site could free up to 1,000 MW, though it is still in development. LifeVal tests everyday tasks like budgeting and paperwork, built from time-use studies and a 3,995-person survey. OpenAI and Anthropic also set up a joint election-monitoring team for the Nov 3 midterms. Grid curtailment matters for capacity assumptions in AI-dependent DR plans.

providers.name: Anthropic
providers.headline: Amended S-1 shows $17B Q3 revenue and $895.4B in purchase commitments; Claude is being abused by malware, and a third Claude Code leader has left since Oct 24.
providers.detail: CNBC reports the revised S-1 discloses $17B in Q3 revenue and $895.4B in purchase commitments, which analysts are scrutinising. Malware was found using Claude to rank stolen victim data. Goldman Sachs restricted Claude Code to engineers. Cat Wu is the third Claude Code departure since Oct 24. Anthropic also opened a paid AI-safety research residency (applications close Nov 22) and confirmed new Claude Code restrictions on copying existing games.
providers.alertReason: Claude API abused by malware to triage stolen data

providers.name: Google Gemini
providers.headline: Google will turn AI features off by default in its school products from 2027 and is widening voluntary buyouts internationally.
providers.detail: Starting in 2027, AI features in Google's education products will default to off, and schools that block AI entirely on their devices also lose search. Buyouts first offered in June now extend to Canada, France, Germany, Japan and Switzerland to offset AI spending. WIRED reported stranded Mount Shasta hikers who relied partly on Gemini for route advice.

providers.name: xAI
providers.headline: Grok 5 missed the Oct 31 market date and has no new release date; Grok 4.7 remains the flagship.
providers.detail: As of Nov 2 there is still no model card, spec sheet or benchmark for Grok 5. Musk's September roadmap puts Grok 4.8 and 4.9 ahead of it. Prediction markets put a release by Dec 31 near a coin flip.

providers.name: Meta
providers.headline: Quiet. No Llama release; Meta reported enforcement against ad accounts tied to a deepfake app network.
providers.detail: WIRED uncovered 400+ deceptive AI apps and sites hiding abusive deepfake tools; Apple pulled 19 apps and Meta acted against the linked ad accounts. No model news.

providers.name: Mistral
providers.headline: Mistral Large 4 is now open weights on Hugging Face: 1T total / 52B active parameters, deployable on-prem.
providers.detail: Mistral calls it the top open model for agentic coding on Artificial Analysis' Coding Agent Index; Terminal-Bench 4.0 rose from 28% to 41%. It has low, medium and high reasoning modes, and Mistral pitches self-hosted threat detection and response. Trained on 3,800 Grace Blackwell GPUs in European data centres. Check the licence terms on the model card before advising clients.

providers.name: Perplexity
providers.headline: Quiet. No new feature or policy change found.
providers.detail: No Perplexity announcements found for late October or early November.

providers.name: Microsoft 365 Copilot
providers.headline: No new ship; the in-app Copilot button rollout in Word, Excel and PowerPoint continues to end of December, with no admin control.
providers.detail: The Copilot button rollout across Windows, macOS and web began in September and should finish by end of December 2026. Microsoft offers no separate admin toggle, so client user-awareness material should account for it.

providers.name: GitHub Copilot
providers.headline: No new ship found.
providers.detail: No GitHub Copilot changelog items found for this window.

providers.name: Cursor
providers.headline: No new ship found; third-party memory tools (beacon.sh) now target Cursor and Claude Code.
providers.detail: beacon.sh released an open-source memory layer that lets coding agents such as Cursor, Claude Code and Codex reuse what they learned in earlier sessions. Nothing new from Cursor itself.

providers.name: Gamma
providers.headline: Still quiet.
providers.detail: No dated Gamma product updates found.

providers.name: Notion AI
providers.headline: No new ship found.
providers.detail: No Notion AI release notes found for this window.

community.signal: Y Combinator's Garry Tan says he spends roughly $100K–$200K a year on AI tokens, which is fuelling debate over what heavy users really spend.
community.so_what: Token cost is now a budgeting line. Include AI consumption in client TCO and continuity-of-service cost models.
